calibration.armEquivalenceCriterion: THE OPERATIONALISATION OF THE OWNER'S "static and DB must produce exactly the same result", written before it was measured (Z-2). Equality is of COMPUTED VALUES over the real cascade, never of emitted-map size: the static arm emits a COMPLETE compiled theme while the DB arm emits a tenant-scoped DELTA that overlays the vertical's base CSS, so the two are different KINDS of output and a map-size or key-set comparison is a category error. knownDefects.finding: MEASURED IN R-2, BEFORE THE CHANGE WAS WRITTEN, and it corrected the implementation. The scope-matched ruling reads 'the probe's DB document declares backgroundMode ALWAYS'; taken as 'on every document', it is unsafe. backgroundMode lives INSIDE palette, so writing it into a document that has no palette node MATERIALISES one. migratePalette then returns a palette patch whose ten seed fields are all undefined, and collectPatchAuthoredPaths collects those ten as AUTHORED keypaths -- including palette.primaryColor, a member of CONSULTED_PROVENANCE_FIELDS. The compiler is thereby told a tenant selected a seed nobody wrote, the governed seed-derivation ladder fires, and channels repaint. Measured: 24 of the 36 receipted DB-arm compiles change VALUE that way (density.mode, spacing.rhythm, surfaces.effect-intensity and experience.profile, on all three verticals), with --ds-button-primary-bg, --ds-button-primary-bg-hover and --ds-color-border-focus among the new rows. knownDefects.resolution: The stamp is scoped to documents that already write a palette node, which is the reading under which the ruling's stated consequence is true. Every control whose door is not a palette keypath builds a byte-identical document to the one it built before R-2. calibration.stopAdmissibilityByVertical: MEASURED IN R-2, and it is a PARTITION rather than a shortlist. Under the scope-matched ruling the DB document declares backgroundMode = the vertical's own defaultMode, so the governed contrast floor is evaluated against that mode's on-primary ink -- which is #0C0C0E on rottay (dark default) and #ffffff on bithire/evnto (light default). A near-black ink demands a LIGHT seed; a white ink demands a DARK one. Measured over a 216-seed sweep of the RGB cube: ZERO seeds are admissible on all three verticals, 79 are rottay-only, 122 are bithire+evnto-only, 15 are admissible nowhere, and the mixed-other bucket is EMPTY -- bithire and evnto always agree with each other and always disagree with rottay. So the roster is per-vertical by construction, not by preference. DB arm: primary/crimson (#DC2626) and primary/indigo (#4F46E5) lower on bithire and evnto and are REFUSED on rottay (APCA Lc 32.2 and 23.2, dark --ds-button-primary-color against --ds-button-primary-bg); primary/warm-sand (#FFD166) and primary/pale-mint (#A7F3D0) lower on rottay and are REFUSED on bithire and evnto (Lc -23.9 and -16.1, light, same pair). Each vertical therefore has exactly TWO DB witnesses, which is what keeps H-2 decidable per arm. STATIC arm: all four lower on all three, because compileBrandTheme has no contrast floor at all -- see ASYMMETRIC_CONTRAST_VALIDATION_BETWEEN_DOORS. primary/identity is a static-arm claim (W-B) and lowers on neither DB vertical: it emits 7 variables and none of the five declared channels.
calibration.modeScopeRecord: WHERE THE SCOPE IS ON THE RECORD, named once so a reader does not excavate it. (i) producedBy.input.modeScope -- the backgroundMode the DB document declared for this run, or null on the static arm and on any DB document with no palette node. (ii) producedBy.input.compilerInput.appearance.palette.backgroundMode -- the same value where it physically travels, inside the input actually handed to compile(). It is NOT in producedBy.input.document, which is the manifest-path-relative shape buildIngressInput built before toCompilerInput reshaped it; W-A asked for this to be verified rather than assumed, and it was (R-2 drill 3). (iii) producedBy.modeChannels -- the per-channel scope census M-1 already emitted: which modes the compiler wrote a block for and which declared channels each one carries. That is the record that tells 'this control has nothing in any mode block' apart from 'this control is governed per mode', and after R-2 it is also what makes an empty base map readable instead of alarming.
calibration.equivalenceClaimScope: THE CLAIM THIS CONTROL MAKES, BOUNDED, AND IT IS NOT 'THE TWO DOORS ARE EQUIVALENT'. What is verified is: EQUIVALENCE FOR THE STOPS ADMISSIBLE ON EACH VERTICAL, UNDER AN EXPLICIT modeScope EQUAL TO THAT VERTICAL'S DEFAULT MODE. Three bounds, each measured rather than assumed. (i) STOPS: only two of the four declared colour stops are admissible per vertical, and the sets are complementary (calibration.stopAdmissibilityByVertical); nothing is claimed for the stops each vertical's contrast floor refuses, and nothing at all is claimed for the identity stop on the DB arm. (ii) SCOPE: every run declares palette.backgroundMode = the vertical's own defaultMode (producedBy.input.modeScope), which is what puts both doors in the same mode in the first place. A tenant document that declares NO backgroundMode is a different scene -- on a dark-default vertical the seed lands in modes.light -- and this control measured that scene only to the extent of naming it (ROTTAY_DB_SEED_LANDS_IN_THE_NON_DEFAULT_MODE.openProductQuestion). (iii) CHANNELS: the equivalence is over the painted diff of the measured fixture roster; three of the five declared channels cannot witness on some vertical for structural reasons (measuredResult.r2BlindWitnesses). THE DOORS ARE NOT SYMMETRIC AND THIS CONTROL SAYS SO: the DB door applies a governed contrast floor that the static door does not have at all, which is why the static arm lowers five witness stops where the DB arm lowers two (ASYMMETRIC_CONTRAST_VALIDATION_BETWEEN_DOORS). A reader may cite these six receipts for the bounded claim above and for nothing wider.

knownDefects.finding: THE INSTRUMENT READ STALE. Measured on the full 14-fixture roster through the probe own measure path: after an inline write on the document element the DEPENDENT computed properties came back ONE PHASE BEHIND -- the mutation read returned the baseline values, the removal read returned the mutation values -- while the custom property itself was always current. runtime/measure/index.mjs already documented this failure mode inside readAll; its offsetHeight flush plus a two-rAF settle was not sufficient at roster size. Evidence: packages/core/artifacts/quality/programs/modern-rescue/archive/cascade-proofs/unreceipted/typography-scale-static-db-residuals/isolation.MEASURED-NOT-RECEIPTED.json.
knownDefects.productionReading: DT ruling, and it SURVIVES the fix rather than being retired by it. The productive DB path compiles on the server and embeds the artifact for SSR, and the client hydrates that exact artifact with visualAuthority=compiled-artifact, so the served artifact carries the tenant RESOLVED values in the artifact scope itself. The probe DB arm models the PREVIEW path (provider-side emission, inline on the document element), which is the compatibility path. H3C fixed WHEN that inline write is delivered, not WHICH path is modelled: the arm is still the preview arm, and whether it should instead serve the compiled artifact remains an open fidelity decision.
knownDefects.remediation: DONE (H3C). The arm keeps its root-inline-style position -- drilled, so adopting the compiled-artifact serving path cannot slip in through this door -- and only the moment of the write changed. Serving the compiled tenant artifact stays an open FIDELITY decision about what the DB arm should model, not a cure for a symptom.

Chain of record, per AA-1: measured and written by the writer (architecture review) across F4B-7, the H-3 design and H-3a; adjudicated by the DT (design authority), who ordered isolate-before-serve; endorsed by independent audit in the H-3 preaudit (AA-1..AA-5).
knownDefects.fix: H-3a: readAll no longer trusts its first answer. It reads, provokes a full style invalidation, and reads again, accepting only after TWO consecutive identical readings, and throwing if the page never settles. Measured effect on this control, same serving model and no cascade change: light-scope divergence fell from 27 rows to 16, and card-modern-md/root now moves 15px -> 14.1px on the DB arm, byte-identical to the static arm. Invariance of the already-closed evidence was measured, not assumed: 36 stored scenarios re-run under the corrected instrument, 26212 shared movement keys compared, ZERO moved values and ZERO changed verdict legs.
knownDefects.residual: CLOSED AT ZERO, and closed by isolating it rather than by declaring it small. H3B put the same single declaration --ds-type-scale: 0.94 on one scene and one bundle through three deliveries: stylesheet-fresh (the static arm) and inline-fresh agree on every reading, while inline-live -- the DB arm as it was then -- diverged. So the residue was never the cascade, the serving model or the arm position: an inline write applied to a LIVE page leaves some elements computed against the old root, and because that state is stable it agrees with itself and the H-3a stability law cannot see it. knownDefects.fixChain: THREE corrections, in order, each one measured before the next was designed. (1) F4B-7: capabilities/index.ts:182 read "typography (ramp channels)", prose that every path walker split on ".", so the static door lowered nothing -- guard 0/1 -> 1/1 on all three verticals. (2) H-3a: readAll stopped trusting its first answer (read, provoke a full style invalidation, read again, accept only after two consecutive identical readings, throw if the page never settles) -- 27 -> 16 divergent light-scope rows. (3) H3C: the DB arm delivers its write to a document that has computed nothing yet, installed before first paint and navigated per phase, exactly as the static arm already navigates -- 16 -> 0. The H-3a law is KEPT: the phase lag it catches is real and separate, and a page computed once agrees with itself immediately, so the law is now cheap rather than redundant.

calibration.negativeControlsScopeNote: Three, and the two that are absent are absent on purpose. "font metrics remain fixed" is what this control MOVES -- binding it would assert that the dial under test must not work. "control height remains fixed" is equally wrong here and for a measured reason rather than a cautious one: the rem root itself derives from this dial (classic/theme.css:22 sets the root font-size from --ds-font-size-base, which is calc(0.9375rem * var(--ds-type-scale, 1))), so every rem-sized control legitimately follows it -- button-modern-md/hitbox moves on both arms, in step. What remains genuinely orthogonal is colour, stroke and motion, and those three are bound at every-measured-target scope, so they are checked on all fourteen fixtures rather than on a chosen few. "border remains fixed" is deliberately NOT the entry used: it bundles the four border-*-radius longhands, which belong to shape.radius-scale, so this control would be asserting about an axis it does not own.
calibration.evidenceKindLabellingRule: One stop per proof role, so both COMPUTED_DELTA and EXACT_RESTORE are carried by real runs rather than by the same run counted twice: compacta is labelled static-db-computed-parity and amplia exact-restore.
